title: CC Compute Manifest
description: Configuration for one compute (job). The core library transforms this into the payload an SDK reads, so field names here differ from the payload's: inputs.payload_attributes becomes payload attributes, inputs.data_sources becomes payload inputs. Both shapes are contract. Field names from cc-home/docs/06_compute-manifest.md.

plugin_definition.description: AWS Batch: '{plugin_name}:{plugin_revision}'. Local Docker: '{plugin_name}', revision omitted.
plugin_definition.x-cc-rule: STD-OPS-001: pinning by revision is what makes a run reproducible. A manifest with no revision resolves to whatever the latest registered revision is at submit time, so the same compute file can produce different results on two days.

command.description: Overrides the registered plugin command for this compute.

dependencies.description: Compute manifest FILENAMES that must succeed first. Any dependency failure fails this job.
dependencies.x-cc-known-divergence: Dependencies are expressed as file paths, relative or absolute, not as manifest_name values. Two manifests with the same manifest_name in different directories are therefore distinguishable, but a moved file silently rewires the DAG. The edge set is defined by filesystem location.

parameters.description: Values substituted for Ref:: placeholders in the plugin manifest command. Maps placeholder name to value. Documented sample uses an integer value, so values are not strings-only.

payload_attributes.x-cc-known-divergence: THREE names for one concept across the system: inputs.payload_attributes in a compute manifest, payloadAttributes in the Confluence payload example, and attributes in the actual serialized payload per cc-go-sdk. Any of the three could be the one a given SDK reads. This is the top-priority parity question for the contracts suite.

tags.description: Passed to the compute provider where supported. Does not affect compute.

job_timeout.description: Seconds; overrides the plugin manifest's execution_timeout.

resource_requirements.description: Resource overrides as key/value pairs, overriding compute_environment.

x-cc-notes.transform-is-contract: The compute-manifest-to-payload mapping is itself part of the wire contract and is currently documented only in prose. A payload fixture is not reproducible from a compute manifest fixture unless the mapping is pinned. contracts/transform/ records the expected mapping.
x-cc-notes.why-two-shapes: A compute manifest is authored by a person and read by the core library; a payload is emitted by the core library and read by every SDK. The authoring shape nests under inputs for readability; the runtime shape is flat. Neither is wrong, but an SDK author reading the docs and an SDK author reading a captured payload will implement two different parsers unless this is stated.
